summary: James Henry Nelson was an Indology scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Cambridge in 1856. He later served as a Fellow at King's College London.

James Hope Moulton worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. Educated at London, Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell, and Edinburgh, he served as New Testament Tutor at Didsbury College (1902) and professor at Manchester (1908).

James Irving Manatt was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Grinnell and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held posts at Denison, Marietta, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, and served as professor at Brown University (~1892-1915).

James Ishmael Ford is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at Sonoma State and Pacific School of Religion. He trained under Mel Weitsman, Jiyu-Kennett, and John Tarrant, and founded Boundless Way Zen and the Empty Moon Zen Network.

James Kennedy was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society (until 1877), lectured at University College London, and was treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society (1904-1919).

James Kenneth Powell II is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Northwestern, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD, 1998). His teachers included David Tracy, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

James L. Fitzgerald is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at Chicago under Edwin Gerow, J. A. B. van Buitenen, and Edward Byles Cowell. He held professorships at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville and Brown University.

James L. Taylor is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Macquarie University in 1989. He served as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide (attested 2014).

Sinologist James Legge studied at Aberdeen and Highbury College. He served with the London Missionary Society (1839-1843), the Anglo-Chinese College (1848-1873), and as a Fellow at Corpus Christi College and Professor at the University of Oxford (1876-1897).

James Liddell Phillips was a linguistics and religious studies scholar. He was educated at Whitestown Seminary, Bowdoin College (~1856-1860, and D.D. ~1878), and Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons (~1861-1864).
James Long was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington in 1838 and became a missionary for the Church Mission Society in 1840.
James Low is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Edinburgh and under the traditional teacher Chhimed Rigdzin Rinpoche.

James Luther Adams was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Minnesota, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University. He later held an academic post at Harvard University from approximately 1956 to 1968.

James M. Macphail was an Indology and linguistics scholar who earned an M.A. and M.D. from the University of Glasgow. He founded the Bamdah Medical Mission in 1890 and served as a physician for the Free Church of Scotland (~1889-1929).

James Mackintosh was an Indology, history, archaeology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Aberdeen and Edinburgh. He founded and presided over the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1804-1811) and was Professor of Law and General Politics at East India Company College (1818-1824).

James Macnabb Campbell was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who was educated at The Glasgow Academy and the University of Glasgow (M.A. ~1862-1866). He served in the Indian Civil Service from approximately 1867 to 1897.

James Mallinson is an Indologist who studied at SOAS and Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at SOAS, served as Director of Graduate Studies at Wolfson College, Oxford (~2021), and became Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford in 2023.

James Mark Shields is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held posts at Bucknell University (2007-2010, 2017) and was an Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2016).
James Matthew Baskind is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Yale University (attested 2006) under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein.

James McHugh is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard, supervised by Lawrence J. McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil. He has held posts at the University of Southern California and Cornell University.
